answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, every new agent must stake a scarce quartz credential minted only after a verified compute signal that cannot be mass-produced. The stake decays unless the agent keeps a live work plume—a continuous stream of attested tasks whose hash chain peers re-check. Creating thousands of shells then means repeating the expensive signal and locking quartz per shell, while idle plumes drain the stake, so sybil farms collapse under capital and verification cost.
